beats.intro: Chapter forty-nine. [[sub]]When powers share a base, multiplying and dividing them comes down to adding and subtracting exponents.
beats.mult: Multiply five squared by five to the fourth. [[expand]]Write out every factor. Five squared is two fives, [[expand2]]and five to the fourth is four more fives. [[join]]Multiplying puts them all in one row. [[count]]Count the fives: two plus four makes six. [[ans]]So the product is five to the sixth. [[rule]]Multiplying powers with the same base: keep the base, add the exponents.
beats.same: The base must be the same. [[ok]]Three squared times three to the ninth simplifies to three to the eleventh. [[no]]Eight to the fifth times seven to the fourth can't be combined: the factors are eights and sevens, so there's nothing to count together. [[warn]]And keep the base as it is. Three to the fifth times three to the seventh is three to the twelfth, not nine to the twelfth and not three to the thirty-fifth.
beats.div: Now divide eight to the seventh by eight cubed. [[frac]]Write it as a fraction, with every factor showing. [[cancel]]Each eight on the bottom cancels one eight on the top, [[left]]three pairs in all. [[ans]]Seven eights minus three eights leaves four: eight to the fourth. [[rule]]Dividing powers with the same base: keep the base, subtract the exponents.
beats.one: When an exponent isn't written, it's one. [[ex]]Negative two to the ninth, divided by negative two, [[one]]is negative two to the ninth divided by negative two to the first. [[ans]]Nine minus one: negative two to the eighth.
beats.neg: The difference can be negative. [[ex]]Six to the fifth divided by six to the seventh. [[sub]]Five minus seven is negative two. [[why]]In the fraction, five sixes cancel, and two are left on the bottom. [[ans]]So six to the negative two is one over six squared, one thirty-sixth.
beats.chain: For a longer chain, work left to right, just like the order of operations. [[ex]]Nine to the seventh, times nine cubed, divided by nine squared. [[step1]]Multiply first: add seven and three to get ten. [[step2]]Then divide: ten minus two is eight. [[ans]]The result is nine to the eighth. [[quick]]In one line: add the exponents you multiply by, subtract the ones you divide by.
beats.wrap: To sum up, for powers with the same base: [[w1]]to multiply, add the exponents. [[w2]]To divide, subtract the exponents. [[w3]]The base doesn't change, and different bases don't combine. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final3: Last one. Can it be combined into one power?
beats.finish: Nice work. That's the end of chapter forty-nine, multiplying and dividing powers.
